source_locator.quote: To reduce the high computational cost of standard quadratic attention, linear attention has been proposed as an efficient approximation. It employs kernel functions that are applied independently to the inputs before the pairwise similarities are calculated. That allows for an efficient computational procedure which, however, amounts to a low-degree rational function approximating softmax.

claims.text: Conventional linear attention reduces the cost of quadratic attention by applying kernels independently before pairwise similarities, but the resulting computation is a low-degree rational approximation to softmax.

source_locator.quote: Unlike previous works on linear attention, the nonlinearity in HLA is not applied separately to queries and keys, but, analogously to standard softmax attention, after the pairwise similarities have been computed.

claims.text: HLA applies its nonlinearity after pairwise query-key similarities rather than separately to queries and keys.

source_locator.quote: An efficient computation scheme for the proposed method is derived that is similar to that of standard linear attention. In contrast to other approaches, no time-consuming tensor reshaping is necessary to apply the proposed algorithm.

claims.text: The paper derives an HLA computation scheme similar to standard linear attention that does not require time-consuming tensor reshaping.

source_locator.quote: The computational complexity of the proposed algorithm is linear with respect to the sequence length. It grows polynomially with the number of factors in the Hadamard product in equation  5 𝒪 ⁡ ( d ϕ F ) \mathcal{O}\left(d_{\phi}^{F}\right) .

claims.text: HLA's computational complexity is linear in sequence length and polynomial in the number of Hadamard factors.

source_locator.quote: We fine-tune our model variants using a 350K subset of the data used by OpenSoraPlan  ( Lin et al., 2024 ) . We also use about 100K synthetic videos generated by Wan2.1 14B.

claims.text: The video-diffusion variants are fine-tuned on a 350K-example OpenSoraPlan subset plus about 100K synthetic videos generated by Wan2.1 14B.

source_locator.quote: We use a learning rate of 1 × 10 − 4 1\times 10^{-4} for all models and all stages and use 8 H100 GPUs.

claims.text: All reported model-training stages use a learning rate of 1e-4 and eight H100 GPUs.

source_locator.quote: We do not compare with recent sophisticated variants of linear attention that use windowing, delta rule or hybrid methods that combine standard linear attention with softmax-attention.

claims.text: The evaluation excludes recent linear-attention variants using windowing, the delta rule, or softmax-linear hybrid methods.

source_locator.quote: As can be seen, the model using the proposed attention mechanism is slightly inferior. Compared with Wan2.1-1.3B, the model it is based on, it has about 23% lower computational complexity (cf. table  2 ).

claims.text: HLA-3F-R1-10 is reported as slightly inferior on VBench to comparable state-of-the-art models while having about 23% lower computational complexity than its Wan2.1-1.3B base model.

source_locator.quote: It can be seen that the VBench scores slightly reduce while the number of HLA layers increases. Conversely, the computational complexity reduces.

claims.text: Across HLA variants, increasing the number of HLA layers slightly reduces VBench scores while reducing computational complexity.

source_locator.quote: Depending on the resolution and the algorithmic variant, HLA requires between 20% and 90% less floating-point operations (FLOPs) than quadratic attention.

claims.text: Depending on resolution and HLA variant, the reported operation count is 20% to 90% lower than quadratic attention.

source_locator.quote: Less capable accelerators, for instance those widely used in mobile applications, can be expected to benefit even more from the proposed algorithm.

claims.text: The paper expects less-capable accelerators used in mobile applications to benefit more from HLA, but presents this as an expectation rather than a measured result.

method: Hadamard Linear Attention applies a multiplicative nonlinearity after query-key pairwise similarities, derives a linear-in-sequence-length computation using standard tensor operations, and substitutes it into selected attention blocks of a Wan2.1 1.3B video-diffusion model.
problem: Standard quadratic attention is expensive for the very long token sequences used in video diffusion, while conventional linear-attention approximations can lose expressiveness through their low-degree formulation.
warnings: The source reports training on eight H100 GPUs but does not state the hardware used for generation-time comparisons, so inference latency is not tied to a specified device.
The projected benefit for mobile accelerators is not supported by a physical mobile-device measurement in the supplied source.
The normalized HTML supplies narrative table references but not the underlying table-cell values, limiting recovery of per-variant VBench scores, FLOP totals, and generation times.
